text:
maya: kick off thread for a prioritized burst "ladder" for reserved pools. idea: deterministic ordering of where burst traffic goes (reserved headroom, borrowed pools, best-effort, preempt) based on tenant SLA tier + contract commitments. want to capture policy, metrics, and GA gating.

ryan: like a fallback chain but with priorities attached to SLA tiers? sounds good. need clear rules for preemption order.

kevin: from infra side, main constraints: fast decision (router-level), low-state, and no cross-region magic. prefer small decision matrix that maps (tenant_tier, current_overcommit_pct) -> route.

sara: product view: tiers = platinum/gold/silver/beta. platinum gets first crack at borrowed pool and reserved headroom, gold next, etc. but we shouldn't promise zero impact for platinum if global pressure. need global budget.

olivia: commercial ask: customers expect documented outcomes. propose we publish a simple ladder graphic and per-tier guarantees for pilot: e.g., platinum: 3m soft headroom + preemption last; gold: 1m soft headroom; silver: no soft headroom, best-effort only. pilot opt-in.

jordan: router logic sketch: at request time compute "priority_score" = f(tier, elapsed_burst_time, backlog). then consult fast policy cache that returns route: reserved_local, reserved_borrowed, best_effort, reject. Cache TTL 2s and periodic sync from policy store.

kevin: implementation detail: prefer token-bucket per-tenant for reserved headroom. borrowed pools count against donor budget; donor budget tracked per-pool with sliding window. If budget insufficient, router returns best_effort.

maya: policy table example for alpha (product doc):
```
priority_ladder:
  - tier: platinum
    headroom_secs: 180
    borrow_allowed: true
    preempt_priority: low
  - tier: gold
    headroom_secs: 60
    borrow_allowed: true
    preempt_priority: medium
  - tier: silver
    headroom_secs: 0
    borrow_allowed: false
    preempt_priority: high
```

ryan: monitoring: need per-tenant counters for headroom_used, borrow_accepted, borrow_revoked, preempt_events. also global metrics: total_reserved_headroom_in_use, total_borrow_in_use.

sara: launch acceptance criteria suggestion:
- pilot with at least 3 customers across platinum/gold/silver
- no more than 5% of platinum requests hitting preempt path during pilot windows
- billing artifacts for headroom/borrow produced and validated
- dashboard tile showing ladder state + per-tenant consumption

olivia: commercial detail: billing for headroom vs borrow. option A: include X seconds per billing period for platinum/gold; overage billed as surge. option B: bill borrowed capacity at a visible premium. finance wants predictable revenue; prefer fixed included headroom.

finance-bot: finance note: if we include headroom, model expected cost delta by tier and cap total included seconds at customer-size percentile to control cost. need CSV export schema: tenant_id, event_ts, type(headroom|borrow), qty_secs, cost_usd.

jordan: safety nets:
- global headroom cap (percent of regional capacity)
- per-tenant concurrency caps when on headroom path
- fast revoke signal to router when donor pool pressure rises

kevin: perf tests planned: microburst hitting single platinum tenant, many silver tenants spiking, donor pool churn. verify no tail latency regression >10% for non-bursting tenants.

maya: UX: Console should surface ladder level, remaining headroom, borrow history, and clear explanations. also a programmatic header X-Burst-Ladder-State for observability. docs to include examples and troubleshooting.

sara: ops runbook items:
- alert when global_headroom > 60% for 5m
- page if more than 3 donor pools hit >80% borrow cap
- mitigation: flip feature flag regionally and revoke borrows

jordan: RFC checklist for eng:
- policy store + short TTL cache in router
- per-tenant token buckets + per-pool donor counters
- metric tags: ladder.tier, ladder.route, ladder.revoked
- stress tests + canary rollout plan

olivia: marketing/sales asks: pilot one-pager describing expected behavior, example invoices, and a short FAQ. sales wants a simple decision tree to explain to customers.

legal-bot: contract note: explicitly call out borrowing across pools and preemption ordering in pilot contracts. recommend opt-in and clear billing language.

maya: timeline proposal:
- wk0: write RFC + policy matrix + billing schema
- wk1-2: infra + routing changes (canary in staging)
- wk3: perf and chaos tests
- wk4: pilot rollout to 3 tenants behind FF
- wk5-6: monitor metrics and iterate on ladder thresholds

kevin: question: how do we handle quota changes mid-burst (customer upgrades/downgrades)? propose recompute headroom cap immediately and adjust token bucket proportionally. add to RFC.

sara: risk log to capture in RFC:
- customer confusion -> bill disputes
- cross-tenant SLO regressions if borrow policy misconfigured
- complexity in debugging multi-hop borrow traffic

maya: mitigations: conservative defaults, pilot opt-in, exportable ledger for every event, visible dashboard, and 30d dispute window.

olivia: ok to start drafting pilot materials after RFC. i'll coordinate with finance/legal.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll assign owners and post RFC link here. tagging @jordan to create pilot channel when we flip flags. :rocket
